memory_update.text: ONTO should remain high on the HBM advanced-packaging sub-supplier watchlist because it has explicit HBM4 selection/order evidence for Dragonfly G5 and 3Di inspection/metrology.
CAMT belongs in the underfollowed inspection/metrology lane; evidence is strong for advanced packaging generally, but HBM-specific customer/order evidence still needs verification.

KLIC is a hypothesis candidate for memory interconnect, thermo-compression, and hybrid bonding exposure; survival to later layers requires proof of production-scale HBM or high-density memory packaging wins.

TSM / CoWoS remains the reference chokepoint anchor; the underfollowed alpha hunt should focus on the yield-control, bonding, metrology, substrate, and test suppliers pulled forward by CoWoS/HBM capacity ramps.

Potential candidates not included due to the 4-name cap but worth future Layer 1B passes: AMKR for OSAT advanced packaging/test, ACMR for advanced packaging wet tools/cleaning if evidence supports it, and substrate/material suppliers if US-listed exposure can be isolated.

summary: Layer 1B expands the HBM / advanced-packaging supplier universe beyond obvious HBM producers. The most useful two-lane map is: one reference anchor that defines the chokepoint, TSMC / CoWoS, and three underfollowed US-listed discovery names tied to inspection, metrology, bonding, and packaging yield control. The strongest discovery evidence in this pass is for Onto Innovation and Camtek, because both connect directly to advanced packaging inspection/metrology, and Onto has explicit HBM4 selection language. Kulicke & Soffa is more hypothesis-driven but relevant because memory-focused thermo-compression and hybrid-bonding tools could become a second-order HBM assembly chokepoint. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
